note: Mechanisms only. No proper names. Case numbers match docs/research/capability-cases-2026-10-14.md, which holds the citations.

U1.name: Investigators and charging
U1.work_order: An investigator (a prosecutor's office, an inspector, an ethics body) that reads kept records (the cash journal, what people know, tips), takes cooperating testimony, files charges, accepts pleas and sets sentences. Each step is a decision from the investigator's own drives, workload and the law in force; nothing is rolled. Courts proper stay after early access, so start with the prosecutor's side and a plea.

U2.name: Surfacing to the press, and the press's choice
U2.work_order: When a person decides to tell, they can tell an outlet. An outlet's editor weighs the story by who it touches, what documents it has and its reach, then runs it or not. A run becomes a public record the news engine carries, with the outlet's trust and slant. Today the 'told' record reaches one listener and no outlet.

U3.name: Voters read scandal as what they heard
U3.work_order: Replace the on/off 'scandal' flag and its flat 5-point penalty with each voter's own knowledge. Counted voter groups hear in the share the news reached, weigh it by their view of the official and their party tie, and forgive more when the official has done them good. Named voters read it too (today they do not).

U4.name: A kept standing measure for each official
U4.work_order: A job-approval-style measure per official, kept by the core from what voters think of them and the economy (this is the open 'electorate approval' stopgap). Recalls, parties, legislators and the press read it. It has to rise and fall by cause.

U5.name: Removal and pressure inside bodies and parties
U5.work_order: Impeach, expel, censure, vote no-confidence, ask a member to withdraw from the ballot. Each member decides from their own count of the votes, their party leader's message and their next election; leaders count heads and tell the member. The rule (majority or two-thirds) is law data.

U6.name: Make the bribe buy something
U6.work_order: Wire the corruption engine to the things that can be bought: a contract award, a permit, a vote, an appointment. The same people repeat the exchange over years, the payer's firm wins or loses the award, the official's cash moves through the journal, and a share can go up to a party. Today no engine asks for a bribe and none sells one.

U7.name: Succession and vacancy contests
U7.work_order: When a head of government dies, resigns or is removed: the acting holder by charter, then the body or the voters choose a successor, with factions in the body counting votes. Replace the 'special election appointee' stand-in with real rules.

U8.name: Campaign money as law-bound flows
U8.work_order: Contributions by kind of source (person, company, party committee, union), each with the legal limit or ban, transfers between committees, reports, and a violation record when a flow breaks the rule. A donor may expect something back later, which U6 can read.

U9.name: Patronage and merit rules
U9.work_order: A hire, promotion or admission 'by connection' beside the merit rule that governs it, with the objecting staffer's note kept, and a hiring ledger an overseer or a court can read. Appointments already weigh whom the appointer knows; this adds the rule they break and the record.

U10.name: Organized blocs and movements
U10.work_order: Congregations, unions, ward organizations and cause groups as organizations with leaders who register, turn out and instruct members, and a movement that grows by contacts, funds itself and can be absorbed by a rival who adopts its program. Drives already has cause groups; this gives them reach into votes.

U11.name: Labor disputes and public pay
U11.work_order: Unions and public employers bargain; a pay limit or a bargaining law changes what members do; a strike stops a service that residents notice. Public pay is law and budget data the jobs engine reads as an outside option for private workers, so a raise or cut shows up in private wages.

U12.name: Insider reports and what happens to the reporter
U12.work_order: A person who sees wrong decides whether to report it up the chain, outside, or to the press; the people above them decide whether to act, bury it or punish the reporter. Retaliation and later vindication are records others read.

U13.name: Oversight bodies, audits and inquiries
U13.work_order: An auditor or inspector that reports on a government's books, a commission that a leader calls to distance themselves, and hearings with sworn testimony. They read records and produce public records that the press, the body and voters read.

U14.name: Clemency
U14.work_order: An executive (president or governor) may pardon or commute, before or after charge. The decision is theirs from their drives and the political cost they read; voters, the party and prosecutors read it afterward.

U15.name: Recall and initiative from performance, with money
U15.work_order: Let a recall start from what an official did or failed at (crime, a deficit, a fee) as well as an ordinance vote, for a state office as well as a local one; signatures cost money, and donors pay; a measure that passes can be undone or reworked by a legislature.

U16.name: Crowds and violence from grievance
U16.work_order: People who share a grievance gather (a protest at city hall, a march) and some act on a grudge against a named official. Both are decisions from the person's drives and what they hold; officials, the press and voters read the crowd or the act.

U17.name: Kin and name inheritance
U17.work_order: A relative of a well-known office-holder starts with some of the name's recognition and warmth and some of its baggage, and the family's wealth and past are readable records. Inherits come through relationships and the surname's known facts, not a bonus number.

U18.name: Tax-bill shock and fiscal substitution
U18.work_order: Households read a new bill (a flat charge, a reassessment, a fee) against their means and decide to refuse to pay or to back a limit; a passed limit changes the local budget and local governments reach for fees instead.

U19.name: Records that stay readable for years
U19.work_order: A dated record (a payment, a vote, a filing) stays indexed and readable for years without a daily scan. It carries the law that applied on its date. A later actor can read it under a later reading of that law, such as a successor prosecutor or an appeal.

D1.name: A flag that flips, with a flat price
D1.why: A candidate is 'tainted' the moment one surfaced record of a taken bribe exists and loses a flat five points from the counted voter groups. It does not depend on how many voters heard of it, how popular the official is, what the economy is doing or how the press treated it. Named voters never read it (voting.ts holds no crime reference). It is a threshold with a constant, which the owner's 'sliding scales' rule forbids; named voters ignoring it also breaks 'an effect is a read'.

D2.name: The bribe engine is built and installed but never asked
D2.where: src/director/play-modules.ts:38 registers it; src/core2/corruption.test.ts is the only caller of considerBribe
D2.why: No engine in play offers or takes a bribe, so a played world holds no corruption record. It also surfaces by one route only (a sour tie), and the 'told' event is not a public record, so the news engine never carries it. Under 'wire to the world' this is an unregistered placeholder until U6 and U2 land.

D3.name: National mood has no approval record
D3.why: The mood is the economy plus a midterm penalty; no record of the president's approval exists to read. Every case with a popular official surviving, or an unpopular one falling, needs U4.

cases.kind: bribery: contractor kickbacks
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: Engineering firms paid cash to one executive through a chain from county to state to national office; a prosecutor squeezed the payers, their testimony made a trial likely, and the official traded resignation for a light plea.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Firms want repeat public work; the official wants cash and gets it from people who owe their business to his office; middlemen skim and carry.
mechanism.money: Cash in envelopes, a fixed share of each contract, over about a decade, through the same few payers.
mechanism.standing: Rose from county to state to national office with the payments continuing; the national party leader was already weakened by his own scandal and wanted him gone.
mechanism.law_in_force: Bribery and extortion statutes plus a tax law that makes unreported income a crime; leniency and immunity let payers trade testimony for safety.
mechanism.act: Repeated cash payments for awards of public engineering work.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The payers, the middlemen and the official; no outsider.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A federal prosecutor who squeezed payers with their own tax exposure; the official's lawyers; the party leader.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Payments began about a decade before; a probe opened in the year of the plea; plea within months of the probe becoming known to the target.
sliding_factors: How many payers would testify and how much leniency each was offered
Whether the official's own party leader still needed him
Weight of documentary evidence against cash-only dealings

cases.kind: bribery: contractor extortion and kickbacks (city)
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A mayor steered water-department work to a friend's firm and leaned on other contractors for payments; years of lost trust, a perjury scandal and a long grand-jury probe ended in a racketeering conviction.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A mayor who rewards his circle; a friend-contractor who wants every large job; outside contractors who pay to stay in the game.
mechanism.money: Large utility contracts steered to one firm; payoffs and subcontract shares passed back up to the mayor's circle.
mechanism.standing: Re-elected once despite earlier allegations; the collapse came when private messages proved a sworn denial false.
mechanism.law_in_force: Perjury, extortion, racketeering and bid-rigging statutes; a department that awards by a bidding rule the mayor could bend.
mechanism.act: Rigging awards and demanding payments from bidders over several years.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Contractors, department staff, the friend; the press suspected, the public heard only pieces.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A multi-year grand jury; reporters who obtained the private messages; the council; voters.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Acts about 2002-2008; indictment 2010; verdict 2013 (five or more years).
sliding_factors: Whether a document (the messages) made denial impossible

cases.kind: bribery: lobbyist gifts for official acts
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A lobbyist bought trips, meals, tickets and donations for a member who then did favors for the lobbyist's clients; the lobbyist's own prosecution made him cooperate, the member's party leaders read the seat as lost and pushed him off the ballot.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A lobbyist paid by clients to win results; a member who likes the perks and the access; staff who carry the asks.
mechanism.money: Gifts, travel, tickets, meals and campaign donations, from the lobbyist's circle, each small, together large.
mechanism.standing: A senior member in a committee that mattered to the clients; the party in a year when it faced its hardest challenge in a decade.
mechanism.law_in_force: Federal bribery and gift rules; disclosure of lobbying; ethics rules on gifts and travel.
mechanism.act: Official acts (a statement in the record, a letter, a vote) in return for gifts and donations.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The lobbyist, the member, staff and clients; later the lobbyist's emails.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Prosecutors with the lobbyist's cooperation; party leaders counting seats; the press; the district's voters.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Acts about 2000-2004; exposure 2004-05; withdrawal from ballot Aug 2006; plea Oct 2006; sentence Jan 2007.
sliding_factors: National swing against the member's party in the election year

cases.kind: bribery: contractor padding in a machine; press exposé
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A ring that controlled the city's contracts, payroll and nominations padded building bills; a member with a grievance leaked the ledgers, a newspaper and cartoonist made the sums legible to people who could not read, voters swept the slate, and a prosecutor outside the machine convicted the boss.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: The ring wants cash and permanent control; contractors want inflated work; a jilted insider wants revenge.
mechanism.money: Bills inflated by a large multiple and the excess split back to the ring.
mechanism.standing: Absolute inside the city organization: nominations, courts, payroll and contracts; weak with the reform press and the state's party.
mechanism.law_in_force: A city charter that put spending in few hands; criminal statutes with no outside auditor reading the books.
mechanism.act: Padded contracts and kickbacks over several years.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The ring, contractors and clerks; many ward leaders suspected.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A rival newspaper and a political cartoonist; a lawyer named special prosecutor; voters at the next election; a court.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Built in the 1860s; leak and exposé in the autumn of 1871; arrest weeks later; conviction 1873.
sliding_factors: Hard numbers (copies of the ledgers) rather than rumor
Reach of the image to non-readers
Whether the prosecutor owed nothing to the machine
Margin by which the slate lost the next election

cases.kind: bribery: system-wide kickbacks; party collapse
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A small-city arrest of a party official who was disowned by his leader made him confess; each confession gave prosecutors the next arrest until the ruling parties could not fill their rolls, and voters chose an outsider.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Parties fund themselves by taking a share of public contracts; firms pay to be allowed to work; a caught man who feels abandoned by his own side talks.
mechanism.money: A fixed percentage of public contracts, collected for the party and for individuals.
mechanism.standing: Dominant coalition for decades; the leader's public disowning of the first man caught turned a loyal subordinate into a witness.
mechanism.law_in_force: Bribery and illegal party financing statutes; pretrial detention that gave prosecutors leverage; parliamentary immunity that was lifted by vote.
mechanism.act: Routine collection of kickbacks tied to contract awards.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Nearly every firm and party treasurer in the sector.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A prosecuting team; the press; the legislature voting on immunity; voters at the next national election.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Practice ran for decades; first arrest in early 1992; parties dissolved 1993-94.
sliding_factors: Whether each new confession lowered the cost of the next
Party leader's reaction to the first arrest
Collapse of the party vote in local elections that followed

cases.kind: bribery: contractor-politician cartel; convictions later voided
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: Plea bargains from cartel contractors convicted a leading politician and removed him from a race; years later higher courts read the procedure as flawed and voided the verdicts without re-deciding guilt.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: State-linked contractors pay for contracts; politicians and parties take shares; defendants trade confessions for sentences.
mechanism.money: Percentages on very large public contracts routed through accounts and intermediaries.
mechanism.standing: A popular ex-leader leading polls; a trial judge whose reputation rose with each conviction.
mechanism.law_in_force: Plea-bargain rules; jurisdiction rules about which court may hear what; rules on a judge's impartiality.
mechanism.act: Cartel payments and kickbacks across many contracts over a decade.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Contractors, intermediaries, party treasurers.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A task force, a trial judge, appeals courts, later a higher court reading the same record under different rules; voters who saw a candidate removed.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Investigation from 2014; convictions 2017-18; annulments from 2021 (years later).
sliding_factors: Whether confessions were read as free or coerced

cases.kind: patronage hiring; consent decree
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A voter's suit made political hiring and firing illegal, the city kept doing it informally, a bribery probe into truck contracts exposed the hiring files, and a judge imposed a monitor.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Ward leaders and the mayor's office pay for precinct work with city jobs; job holders owe their jobs and work for the organization.
mechanism.money: Salaries from the public payroll as payment for campaign work and turnout; bribes from firms for contracts.
mechanism.standing: A machine with decades of electoral wins; its enforcement was by an honor system.
mechanism.law_in_force: A consent decree banning political firing and hiring for non-policy jobs; contempt power.
mechanism.act: Hiring and promoting on recommendation from party officials, with the paper trail disguised.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Department heads, ward committee members, the job holders themselves.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A federal prosecutor reading hiring files; the plaintiff's lawyer; a judge with contempt power; the press.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Decree 1972 and 1983; exposure of violations 2004-05; monitor after contempt (decades).
sliding_factors: How much of the decree was enforced by anyone other than the plaintiff
Whether a separate crime probe made the files readable

cases.kind: nepotism: admissions favoritism for the connected
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: Trustees, legislators and donors put names on a tracking list; staff objected and were overruled; a newspaper obtained the list and a governor-named panel got sworn testimony that ended the careers of the administrators who ran it.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Officials and donors want favors for friends; administrators want budgets and goodwill from the people who vote on them.
mechanism.money: No cash; favors exchanged for budget support and appointments.
mechanism.standing: The governor who benefited was already discredited; administrators depended on the same trustees.
mechanism.law_in_force: Admission rules written as merit-based; public-records and sworn-testimony powers of an appointed panel.
mechanism.act: Admitting applicants over staff objection because of who asked.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Admissions staff and the administrators who added names.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A newspaper that got the list; a panel with subpoena-like power; legislators; the trustees who appointed the heads.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Practice ran for years; press and hearings within weeks of publication.
sliding_factors: Whether a governor was already discredited
Whether staff objections were written down
Whether the heads depended on the people who made the requests

cases.kind: campaign-finance violation; conviction later reversed
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A political committee collected corporate money that state law barred from candidates, sent it to a party committee, which sent the same total to chosen legislative candidates; a prosecutor read matching amounts and dates as laundering, a jury agreed, and appeals courts later read the statute narrowly.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A party leader wants a legislative majority; corporate donors want influence they cannot buy directly.
mechanism.money: A committee's corporate-source dollars swapped for the same number of dollars of permitted money sent to candidates.
mechanism.standing: Majority leader of the national chamber, with a record of winning.
mechanism.law_in_force: State law forbidding corporate contributions to candidates; money-laundering statute defined by 'proceeds of crime'.
mechanism.act: The swap of funds through a party committee to hide the corporate source.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Committee staff, the party committee, the donors; the dates and amounts were in public filings.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A county prosecutor; a civil plaintiff's discovery; a jury; two layers of appeals reading the same facts under the statute's wording.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Act 2002; indictment about 3 years; verdict about 8 years; reversal 11 years.
sliding_factors: Wording of the statute (proceeds of a crime or not)
Partisan alignment of the prosecutor and the reviewing panel
Evidence that the two flows were linked rather than coincident

cases.kind: campaign-finance: ad contracts kicked back to a party; inquiry; election loss
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A government paid ad firms linked to its own party large commissions for little work; an auditor's report and a new leader's inquiry put sworn testimony on television, opposition parties read it as grounds to bring the government down, and voters cut its seats.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A party wants funds and presence in a restive province; firms want contracts; officials want to please the party.
mechanism.money: Hundreds of millions in program spending of which about a third went to fees and commissions to linked firms.
mechanism.standing: A long-governing party; a new leader who wanted distance from his predecessor.
mechanism.law_in_force: Procurement rules; an independent auditor with a duty to report; inquiry powers; a confidence rule that lets a minority government fall.
mechanism.act: Awarding sponsorship contracts without real work and routing commissions back to the party.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Senior officials, firm owners, party organizers.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: The auditor; the new leader (called the inquiry to distance himself); the televised hearings; opposition parties; voters.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Program 1996-2001; first report 2002; second 2004; inquiry report late 2005; confidence vote and election two months later.
sliding_factors: Government's seat count (minority or majority) at the confidence vote
Opposition parties' view of the polls
Whether the inquiry's televised testimony was heard widely

cases.kind: recall that succeeded (governor)
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A governor re-elected months earlier saw approval collapse over a budget deficit and fee increases; a wealthy backer paid for signatures, a same-ballot slate of replacements made removal feel safe, and a majority removed him.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Voters angry about costs and services; a rival with money; replacement candidates who want the seat.
mechanism.money: A backer's spending on a signature drive; the state's deficit and a fee increase that landed on households.
mechanism.standing: Approval in the low twenties against more than half voting to remove.
mechanism.law_in_force: A state constitution that lets voters recall any statewide official with signatures and puts the replacement vote on the same ballot.
mechanism.act: A recall petition qualified and then voted.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone: fees and deficits are public.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters; the press; the governor's own party, which had no strong alternative.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Re-elected Nov 2002; recall vote Oct 2003 (under a year).
sliding_factors: Whether a credible replacement was on the same ballot

cases.kind: recall that failed (governor), after a labor law
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A law limiting public-employee bargaining brought huge protests and an organized recall with 900,000+ signatures; the electorate that showed up matched the one that elected the governor, and he won by a slightly larger margin.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Public-sector unions lose bargaining rights and dues; supporters of the law see overdue reform; many voters object to recalling without crime.
mechanism.money: Union dues cut; large outside spending on both sides.
mechanism.standing: A governor with a committed base and a majority legislature of his party.
mechanism.law_in_force: A recall allowed by the constitution; a law that ended automatic dues and limited bargaining.
mechanism.act: Passing the law; collecting signatures; the vote.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters in a polarized state; the press; donors.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Law 2011; recall election 2012 (months).
sliding_factors: Whether the electorate at the recall matched the original electorate
Share who opposed recalls on principle

cases.kind: ballot measure overturned a legislature; labor dispute
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A law cutting public-sector bargaining was suspended when citizens gathered about 1.3 million signatures; unions and allies knocked on a million doors and the referendum repealed it by a wide margin.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Police, firefighters, teachers and their families feel a law threatens pay and safety staffing; voters side with them.
mechanism.money: Over thirty million dollars raised by the repeal side; bargaining rights as the stake.
mechanism.standing: A new governor and legislature with a majority; popular sympathy for the workers affected.
mechanism.law_in_force: A state referendum procedure that suspends a law once enough signatures are filed; a simple majority repeals.
mechanism.act: Collecting signatures, campaigning, voting.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters; the legislature that must accept the result.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Law spring 2011; vote Nov 2011.
sliding_factors: Gap between early polls and the result
Which public workers the law named

cases.kind: whistleblower; agency cover-up; outside researchers
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A cost-saving switch in water source left pipes unprotected; a federal staffer's memo and independent researchers' data were dismissed by state agencies until doctors' blood-lead results made it undeniable, then a governor replaced officials and later faced charges.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Managers appointed to cut costs; state regulators who defend their own tests; a staffer, a professor and a pediatrician who read the same facts differently.
mechanism.money: Cost savings from switching source versus the later cost of repair and health harm.
mechanism.standing: Residents poor and with little pull on the state; the regulators were the officials the governor relied on.
mechanism.law_in_force: Environmental rules on lead and treatment; emergency-manager law that took power from local elected officials.
mechanism.act: Switching source without corrosion control; dismissing contrary data.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Plant operators, regulators, a federal staffer (from mid-2015); parents noticed smell and color first.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A professor's sampling; a hospital's lead records; the press; the governor's task force; prosecutors years later.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Switch spring 2014; memo mid-2015; admission autumn 2015; resignations Dec 2015; charges 2021.
sliding_factors: Whether independent measurements existed that contradicted the official ones
Reach of local and national press

cases.kind: press exposé that ended a career
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A front-running candidate who dared reporters to follow him was staked out after a tip; a published story and a photograph in days dried up money and staff and ended the campaign within the week.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Reporters read a dare and a tip as permission; donors and staff want a winner without risk.
mechanism.money: Contributions fell off at once.
mechanism.standing: Front-runner for the nomination; the party's voters had little attachment beyond his lead.
mechanism.law_in_force: None; norms of what the press may publish about private conduct.
mechanism.act: A private act made public by surveillance.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The candidate, a few friends; a tipster.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A newspaper; a tabloid; donors; voters in the first primary state.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Days.
sliding_factors: Candidate's own denial that a document then contradicted
Time left before the first vote

cases.kind: press exposé that fizzled
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A major newspaper reported low tax payments and heavy debt of a candidate; voters who had already decided read it through their party and the poll lead did not move.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Voters hold strong prior views of the candidate; the opponent amplifies the story.
mechanism.money: Reported tax paid near zero in many years; large debts.
mechanism.standing: A divided electorate with few undecided voters in the final weeks.
mechanism.law_in_force: Tax law that allows legal deductions and losses; no rule requiring disclosure.
mechanism.act: Legal conduct that looks bad.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The candidate's accountants; the leak provider.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Readers of the paper, partisans on both sides, the opposing campaign.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: One month before the vote.
sliding_factors: Whether readers of the outlet were already persuaded

cases.kind: scandal survived by a popular official
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A strong economy and a public that read the investigation as overreach kept the president's approval high through impeachment, rewarded his party at the midterm, and left the upper chamber short of the two-thirds needed to remove him.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Opposition-party members want removal; most voters want the economy to hold and distrust the prosecutor.
mechanism.money: None directly; a strong economy.
mechanism.standing: High approval at the start and higher at the end; party divided on strategy, not on loyalty.
mechanism.law_in_force: Impeachment by simple majority in one chamber and removal by two-thirds in the other.
mechanism.act: Private conduct and a sworn denial; a prosecutor's report to the legislature.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone by the report's publication.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A prosecutor; the lower chamber; the upper chamber; voters at a midterm; pollsters.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Conduct 1995-97; report Sept 1998; impeachment Dec 1998; acquittal Feb 1999.

cases.kind: scandal survived: conviction, then re-election
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A mayor caught in a sting served time, then won a ward seat by a landslide and the mayoralty four years later against an unpopular successor, because his base read the sting as entrapment and the city's voters wanted him over the alternative.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A base that credits him with jobs and respect; voters who see the sting as unfair; an unpopular incumbent.
mechanism.money: None directly; city jobs and contracts for supporters.
mechanism.standing: Deep loyalty in one part of the city; citywide popularity had fallen.
mechanism.law_in_force: Possession charges; a sting by federal agents; no bar on a convicted person standing again after sentence.
mechanism.act: Drug use recorded on video.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The informant, the agents; then everyone.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A jury (partial conviction); the ward's voters; the citywide electorate.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Arrest Jan 1990; sentence 1991; ward seat 1992; mayor 1994.
sliding_factors: Whether a base read the act as entrapment

cases.kind: resignation of a chief executive
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A court ordered recordings handed over, one tape proved the president had lied, and senators of his own party counted votes and told him he would be convicted, so he resigned.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A president wants to survive; his party's senators want to survive the next election and protect the party's name.
mechanism.money: None needed.
mechanism.standing: Approval collapsed over two years; his party's leaders held the votes that decided removal.
mechanism.law_in_force: Impeachment and two-thirds removal; a court rule that an executive cannot shield evidence in a criminal case.
mechanism.act: Directing a cover-up and lying about it.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Aides; the recordings held the truth.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A special prosecutor; a court; the lower chamber's committee; party leaders counting votes in the upper chamber; the press and the public.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Break-in June 1972; court order July 1974; tape Aug 5; resignation Aug 9, 1974.
sliding_factors: Number of upper-chamber votes still with him (12 to 15)
A court order that removed his last legal shield

cases.kind: expulsion from a legislature
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: After a jury convicted a member of bribery, racketeering and tax evasion, the ethics panel found nine violations and recommended expulsion, and the full chamber voted nearly unanimously to expel him.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Members want to protect the body's name and have no loyalty to a convicted colleague who had few allies.
mechanism.money: A monthly kickback from a staffer; unreported income.
mechanism.standing: Isolated in his own party and chamber.
mechanism.law_in_force: A two-thirds vote to expel; an ethics committee that investigates and recommends.
mechanism.act: Taking kickbacks and obstructing justice.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Staff and prosecutors.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A jury; the ethics committee; the full chamber.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Conviction in April; expulsion in July of the same year.

cases.kind: pardon
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: An unelected successor pardoned his predecessor before any charge, most voters read it as a deal, approval fell about twenty points at once and his party lost heavily at the midterm, with the memory fading over a decade.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A successor wants to end a divisive trial; voters want accountability.
mechanism.money: None.
mechanism.standing: Approval over 70 percent before; he had never been elected to national office.
mechanism.law_in_force: An unreviewable power to pardon federal offenses, available before charge.
mechanism.act: A pardon a month after the resignation.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: A few aides; announced publicly on a Sunday.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Pollsters, the opposition party, the press, voters at the next two elections.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Immediate drop; midterm two months later; presidential election two years later.
sliding_factors: Time (the same poll turned positive a decade later)

cases.kind: sudden death in office and local succession
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A mayor was killed by a former board member he refused to reappoint; the charter made the board's president acting mayor that day, the board then elected her permanent mayor by the narrowest majority, and the crisis appointment became incumbency.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A former member wants his seat back and reads the refusal as a personal wrong; board members want stability and their own standing.
mechanism.money: None.
mechanism.standing: The board president held the post because of an earlier internal vote.
mechanism.law_in_force: A charter naming the board's president as next in line and letting the board elect a mayor to finish the term.
mechanism.act: A killing; a succession vote a week later.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Nobody beforehand; the grudge was known to colleagues.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: The charter's clerk; the board's members; voters at the next election.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Acting mayor same day; board vote one week; election at term end.

cases.kind: sudden death in office; contested succession
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A mayor's sudden death with no clear heir let a council split between his reform bloc and the old organization pick a compromise successor overnight; crowds read it as the machine's return and demanded a special election.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Reform supporters want continuity; old-organization aldermen want patronage back; the compromise candidate wants the job.
mechanism.money: City jobs and contracts at stake.
mechanism.standing: The dead mayor had a base but not a controlling council bloc.
mechanism.law_in_force: A rule that the council elects an interim mayor from its members; a clerk served for a week first.
mechanism.act: The vote.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone in the room; the crowd outside.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: The council; crowds; the press; voters at the next primary.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Death Nov 25; clerk interim a week; vote Dec 2; next primary 17 months later.
sliding_factors: Time left before the next election

cases.kind: demagogue's rise from a movement
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A governor used state appointments, contracts and a loyal legislature to build a machine, then turned mass anger at a depression into a national club movement with a simple program; he used state power against a judge and was killed by the judge's relative, after which the opposing president took in much of the program.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Voters in a depression want relief and someone to blame; the leader wants national office; local foes want him stopped.
mechanism.money: State jobs, roads and hospitals; a program capping fortunes; club dues and mailings.
mechanism.standing: Control of nominations and the legislature at home; a national audience on the radio.
mechanism.law_in_force: State powers of appointment and districting; a legislature that follows a single leader.
mechanism.act: Building a program and clubs; redrawing a district to unseat a judge.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Press and rivals knew the methods; members knew the program.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters; a rival national leader who absorbed the ideas; a relative of the judge.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Rise over seven years; the final act within days of the redistricting plan.
sliding_factors: Whether a rival absorbed the program
Personal grievance of a target's family

cases.kind: dynasty's second generation riding a movement
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A candidate who had lost a brother told a crowd of a leader's killing in plain words, kept one city calm that night, and carried a coalition of Black and white working-class voters to primary wins until he was shot, after which delegates went to party organizers.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A crowd that hasn't heard the news; a speaker who shares a loss; voters who read him as the one person who can span two groups.
mechanism.money: A family's name, network and funds.
mechanism.standing: Brother of a martyred president; late entrant against a sitting president's stand-in.
mechanism.law_in_force: Primary rules that let a candidate win states; convention delegates held by party organizers in states without primaries.
mechanism.act: An unscripted speech, and then primaries.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The crowd learned of the killing from him.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: The crowd; the press that carried the speech; primary voters; party organizers.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Speech Apr 4; primary May 7; assassination June 5-6.
sliding_factors: Size of the audience (about 2,500) and press carriage
Whether the other campaigns were in the same state
Share of delegates controlled by organizers

cases.kind: dynasty return; online campaign
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: The son of an ousted ruler won by double his rival's votes after a campaign that reshaped the family's story online and allied with a popular outgoing president's family, while decades-old wealth cases stalled in court.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Voters tired of the current order read the old regime as stable; a family wants its name restored.
mechanism.money: Family wealth that recovery cases never reached; campaign money; media production.
mechanism.standing: A defeated runner-up six years earlier; a running mate with a regional base.
mechanism.law_in_force: A single-term presidency; slow civil forfeiture cases; election authorities with no power over false claims.
mechanism.act: A campaign that rewrote the record online.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Viewers received claims; researchers tracked them.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters; fact-checkers; courts that had not acted.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Regime ended 1986; return in 2022 (36 years).
sliding_factors: Alliance with a base in another region
Reach of social media versus press

cases.kind: dynasty heir; influence-peddling scandal; impeachment
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: The daughter of a former ruler, elected on that name, gave an unelected friend access to speeches and documents and helped extract money from conglomerates; a television broadcaster read leaked files, parliament impeached and the top court removed her unanimously.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A president who trusts one person outside government; firms that pay for favors; a broadcaster with documents.
mechanism.money: Funds from large firms to foundations controlled by the friend.
mechanism.standing: Elected on a family name; approval collapsed once the files aired.
mechanism.law_in_force: Impeachment by a legislative supermajority then a court's ruling; bribery and abuse-of-power statutes.
mechanism.act: Sharing state documents and soliciting payments through the friend.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Aides and executives of the paying firms.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A broadcaster, then massive street protests, parliament, prosecutors, the court.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Acts 2013-2016; broadcast Oct 2016; impeached Dec; removed Mar 2017; verdicts 2018-2021.
sliding_factors: Whether the president's own party defected in the impeachment vote

cases.kind: faith-driven vote bloc
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: Pastors registered church members around school, tax and moral issues, evangelicals who had backed a born-again candidate in one election moved about twenty-five points in the next, and the effect varied with how strongly the local organizing reached them.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Church leaders read policies as threats to their schools and values; members trust their pastor and congregation.
mechanism.money: Direct-mail lists and church-based registration drives.
mechanism.standing: A previous candidate from the same faith who lost them on policy.
mechanism.law_in_force: Tax rules for religious schools; voter registration rules that permit church drives.
mechanism.act: Registration and turnout drives through congregations.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Members hear at services.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Members; the campaign that courted them.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Organized in 1979; vote in 1980.
sliding_factors: Alignment of the candidate's faith with the voters'

cases.kind: press exposé shifting a faith-heavy bloc; turnout composition
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A newspaper's report of allegations that a candidate pursued teenagers divided voters by whether they believed it: about half did and almost all of them chose his opponent, while small rural counties of the candidate's own party turned out far less and Black voters turned out heavily.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Voters weigh allegations against party and faith loyalty; organizers push turnout in one group.
mechanism.money: Campaign spending; late national party support.
mechanism.standing: A candidate well known and popular among evangelical voters; an opponent with a prosecutor's record.
mechanism.law_in_force: A special-election date set by the governor; ballot access.
mechanism.act: A report published weeks before the vote.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Women involved and a few contacts; the newspaper after months of work.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters (52 percent said the claims were probably true); county party leaders; national party.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Report Nov 9; vote Dec 12.
sliding_factors: Belief in the claim split by group
Turnout drop by county type (about 37 percent overall)

cases.kind: labor dispute that swung an election
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A government pay limit met strikes by public-sector workers through a cold winter; satisfaction with the government fell to 17 percent, a no-confidence motion passed by one vote and the opposition won a clear majority.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Unions reject a pay limit that falls behind prices; voters read strikes as a government that cannot govern.
mechanism.money: A five percent wage guideline against higher inflation.
mechanism.standing: A minority government dependent on small parties' votes.
mechanism.law_in_force: A confidence rule that brings down a government by majority vote.
mechanism.act: Strikes by truck drivers, council and hospital workers.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone; services stopped.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters; small parties; the opposition.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Strikes Dec 1978-Feb 1979; confidence vote 28 March; election 3 May.
sliding_factors: Unemployment as the opposition's campaign point

cases.kind: tax revolt; party removes its leader
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A flat per-adult local tax replaced a property-based one; non-payment spread, a large demonstration ended in riots, her own party's members of the legislature read polls as losing their seats, forced a second leadership ballot, and cabinet colleagues told her to go.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Households with several adults pay more; the party's members of the legislature in marginal seats fear defeat.
mechanism.money: A flat per-adult charge instead of a rate on property value; non-payment in some areas at 30 percent.
mechanism.standing: Long-serving leader with a strong majority but falling poll lead.
mechanism.law_in_force: A local tax law; party rules for challenging a leader with a vote threshold.
mechanism.act: Non-payment, protest, and a leadership challenge.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Members of the legislature; cabinet ministers; the party's rules.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Introduced 1989-90; riot March 1990; resignation Nov 1990.
sliding_factors: First-ballot margin short of the party threshold

cases.kind: tax revolt by ballot measure
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: Rising home assessments in a decade of inflation left homeowners with tax bills they could not pay while the legislature did nothing; an initiative capped the property tax and limited growth, passed by about two to one and cut local property revenue by more than half, pushing local governments to fees.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Homeowners, especially on fixed incomes, see tax bills double; an organizer turns the grievance into a ballot text.
mechanism.money: Property tax revenue fell by over half; local governments substituted fees and special charges.
mechanism.standing: Legislature slow to give relief; voters enthusiastic.
mechanism.law_in_force: A constitutional initiative that needs only a majority; a two-thirds vote for local special taxes afterward.
mechanism.act: Signatures, campaign, vote.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Every owner got a bill.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters; local councils that then had to cut or raise fees; the state, which backfilled schools.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Assessments surged through the 1970s; vote June 1978; revenue fall within a year.

cases.kind: public-salary scandal; press exposé; recall and law change
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A small city's manager and part-time council set salaries many times their peers' and no outside body read the numbers until a reporter requested the records; within days the state's attorney general subpoenaed files and within ten weeks charged eight officials.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Insiders vote themselves pay; residents in a poor city have little time to watch; a reporter requests records.
mechanism.money: A top salary of about three-quarters of a million dollars; council pay for part-time seats; later restitution in the millions.
mechanism.standing: A council re-elected in low-turnout races; residents with little organization.
mechanism.law_in_force: Open-records law; a charter city's right to set its own pay; criminal misappropriation statutes.
mechanism.act: Voting the pay and hiding it.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The insiders only.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A newspaper; the state attorney general; the courts; residents (recall).
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Years of pay; July 2010 story; subpoena in 11 days; charges in about 10 weeks; sentences 2014.
sliding_factors: Whether a pay table was public

cases.kind: public-salary change that moves private wages
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A large one-time raise to government pay raises the outside option of skilled workers and so may raise private wages where labor markets are tight, though in a slack market the spillover was reported as small.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Skilled workers compare public and private pay and may quit or hold out; private firms match only if short of staff.
mechanism.money: A pay raise for several million public employees, with arrears paid in a lump.
mechanism.standing: Not applicable.
mechanism.law_in_force: A commission recommends and the government adopts pay scales for its own staff.
mechanism.act: Adopting the scales.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone: pay scales are public.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Job seekers, private employers, the budget.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Effect on private wages: unmeasured in sources found.
sliding_factors: Share of workers in the public sector
Size of the existing public premium

cases.kind: selling an appointment; impeachment and removal; commutation
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A governor with sole power to fill a vacant national seat was recorded trying to trade it; arrest came before the appointment, the legislature impeached and removed him almost unanimously within weeks, and a later president cut the sentence.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A governor wants jobs, money and office in return; the legislature wants to preserve its standing and the state's name.
mechanism.money: Offers of an appointment for campaign money or a post.
mechanism.standing: Unpopular and without allies in his own party; the legislature's majority was of his own party.
mechanism.law_in_force: Governor's sole power to appoint to a vacant seat; wiretap authority; impeachment by simple majority and removal by two-thirds of the upper chamber; clemency by a later chief executive.
mechanism.act: Soliciting benefits in return for the appointment.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The governor's circle; prosecutors had a recording.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Prosecutors; the lower chamber (114-1); the upper chamber (59-0); a later president.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Arrest Dec 2008; removal Jan 2009; trials 2010-11; commutation 2020.
sliding_factors: A later president's view of the case

cases.kind: fiction: populist rise, machine use and fall (mechanism only)
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A local official used as a decoy learns he was a pawn, turns to blunt appeals to ordinary people, wins the governorship, rules by contracts and favors, and falls when an aide's dirt on a rival and a private affair each push a relative of the harmed party to act.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: A once-honest man who has learned that reasonable appeals lose; an aide who digs up damaging facts; relatives who act on a private wrong.
mechanism.money: Public contracts and a large public hospital; favors for backers.
mechanism.standing: Strong mass following, weak among the old elite.
mechanism.law_in_force: Governor controls contracts and a compliant legislature.
mechanism.act: Pressure on an opponent with an old secret; a love affair.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: The aide, the targets.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: The target's relatives; the aide.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: A few years; fall in a day.

cases.kind: fiction: old machine mayor's last campaign (mechanism only)
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: An aging mayor whose machine runs on jobs, favors and personal contact loses to a young rival when a publisher opposes him, the old establishment funds the rival, younger voters no longer need his favors and television changes how campaigns reach them.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Voters repay favors with loyalty; a publisher dislikes the mayor; younger voters want other things.
mechanism.money: City jobs and small favors; the establishment's funds for the rival.
mechanism.standing: A long incumbency in immigrant wards; weak with the old establishment.
mechanism.law_in_force: City hiring and contracts in the mayor's gift.
mechanism.act: Campaigning on personal contact; the paper's endorsement of the rival.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters; a nephew who observes.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: One campaign.
sliding_factors: Share of voters who still depend on favors

cases.kind: journalism film: an investigative team targets an institution (mechanism only)
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: A new editor points a reporting team at the institution instead of individual abusers; court records and survivors show that leaders knew and moved offenders for years, readers respond with their own accounts, and the leader resigns within the year.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: An editor who wants institutional answers; survivors who want to be heard; leaders who want to protect the institution.
mechanism.money: Sealed settlements paid quietly.
mechanism.standing: An institution with great local standing and many allies in law and media.
mechanism.law_in_force: Sealed court settlements, then an unsealing motion; public-records rules.
mechanism.act: Transferring offenders and sealing settlements.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Church leaders, lawyers, some reporters earlier.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Readers who called in; prosecutors; the institution's head.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Practice for decades; investigation months; resignation within a year of publication.
sliding_factors: Number of survivors who came forward
Whether sealed documents could be unsealed

cases.kind: recall that succeeded (local prosecutor)
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: Business donors and neighborhood groups who read crime numbers as the prosecutor's failure paid for signatures, the recall went on a low-turnout primary ballot, a majority removed him, and the mayor named the successor.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Residents and businesses who fear crime; donors who object to the prosecutor's policy; the prosecutor's allies who outspend less.
mechanism.money: About nine million dollars across both sides; the largest committee funded by a few donors.
mechanism.standing: Elected on a reform platform in a city with a strong progressive lean but a wave of safety complaints.
mechanism.law_in_force: City charter recall with signatures; vacancy filled by the mayor's appointment.
mechanism.act: Gathering signatures, campaigning, vote.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Everyone: crime and policy are public.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: Voters (55 to 45); the mayor.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Elected 2019; recall vote June 2022.

cases.kind: whistleblower
cases.mechanism_one_sentence: Officers who reported graft to superiors and city officials were ignored for years by supervisors who benefited, until a reporter's series made it a political danger for the mayor, who created a commission; hearings changed the commissioner and the rules.

mechanism.drives_views_relationships: Honest officers want it to stop; supervisors protect their own income; a mayor wants to avoid blame.
mechanism.money: Regular payoffs from illegal businesses, split by squads.
mechanism.standing: The whistleblowers were low-ranking and isolated; the force's culture punished them.
mechanism.law_in_force: No outside body had authority to investigate the police; a mayor could create a commission.
mechanism.act: Taking regular payoffs and ignoring complaints.
mechanism.who_could_have_known: Squad members; supervisors; some city officials.
mechanism.what_read_it_afterward: A reporter's series; the mayor; public hearings; a new commissioner.
mechanism.delay_between_act_and_consequence: Years of internal reports; the series; a commission within weeks; hearings a year and a half later.
